This can be after:\n\nAfter the user's session has expired for any reason:\n\n- User has signed out on another device.\n- The session has reached its timebox limit or inactivity timeout.\n- User has signed in on another device with single session per user enabled.\n- Check the [User Sessions](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/sessions) docs for more information.\n\n&#96;TOKEN_REFRESHED&#96;\n\nIt's best practice and highly recommended to extract the access token (JWT) and store it in memory for further use in your application.\n\n- Avoid frequent calls to&#96;supabase.auth.getSession()&#96; for the same purpose.\n\n&#96;USER_UPDATED&#96;\n\n- Emitted each time the&#96;supabase.auth.updateUser()&#96; method finishes successfully. Listen to it to update your application's UI based on new profile information.\n\n&#96;PASSWORD_RECOVERY&#96;\n\n- Emitted instead of the&#96;SIGNED_IN&#96; event when the user lands on a page that includes a password recovery link in the URL.\n- Use it to show a UI to the user where they can [reset their password](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/passwords#resetting-a-users-password-forgot-password).\n\n### Parameters\n\ncallbackfunction\n\nA callback function to be invoked when an auth event happens.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nobject\n\nDetails\n\nListen to auth changesListen to sign outStore OAuth provider tokens on sign inUse React Context for the User's sessionListen to password recovery eventsListen to sign inListen to token refreshListen to user updates\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((event, session) =\u003e {2  console.log(event, session)34  if (event === 'INITIAL_SESSION') {5    // handle initial session6  } else if (event === 'SIGNED_IN') {7    // handle sign in event8  } else if (event === 'SIGNED_OUT') {9    // handle sign out event10  } else if (event === 'PASSWORD_RECOVERY') {11    // handle password recovery event12  } else if (event === 'TOKEN_REFRESHED') {13    // handle token refreshed event14  } else if (event === 'USER_UPDATED') {15    // handle user updated event16  }17})1819// call unsubscribe to remove the callback20data.subscription.unsubscribe()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Create an anonymous user\n\n&#96;signInAnonymously(credentials?)&#96;\n\nCreates a new anonymous user.\n\n- Returns an anonymous user\n- It is recommended to set up captcha for anonymous sign-ins to prevent abuse. You can pass in the captcha token in the&#96;options&#96; param.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentials\n\nOptional\n\nSignInAnonymouslyCredentials\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nCreate an anonymous userCreate an anonymous user with custom user metadata\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInAnonymously({2  options: {3    captchaToken4  }5});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Sign in a user\n\n&#96;signInWithPassword(credentials)&#96;\n\nLog in an existing user with an email and password or phone and password.\n\nBe aware that you may get back an error message that will not distinguish between the cases where the account does not exist or that the email/phone and password combination is wrong or that the account can only be accessed via social login.\n\n- Requires either an email and password or a phone number and password.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsSignInWithPasswordCredentials\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign in with email and passwordSign in with phone and password\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({2  email: 'example@email.com',3  password: 'example-password',4})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Sign in with ID token (native sign-in)\n\n&#96;signInWithIdToken(credentials)&#96;\n\nAllows signing in with an OIDC ID token. The authentication provider used should be enabled and configured.\n\n- Use an ID token to sign in.\n- Especially useful when implementing sign in using native platform dialogs in mobile or desktop apps using Sign in with Apple or Sign in with Google on iOS and Android.\n- You can also use Google's [One Tap](https://developers.google.com/identity/gsi/web/guides/display-google-one-tap) and [Automatic sign-in](https://developers.google.com/identity/gsi/web/guides/automatic-sign-in-sign-out) via this API.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsSignInWithIdTokenCredentials\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign In using ID Token\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithIdToken({2  provider: 'google',3  token: 'your-id-token'4})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Sign in a user through OTP\n\n&#96;signInWithOtp(credentials)&#96;\n\nLog in a user using magiclink or a one-time password (OTP).\n\nIf the&#96;{{ .ConfirmationURL }}&#96; variable is specified in the email template, a magiclink will be sent. If the&#96;{{ .Token }}&#96; variable is specified in the email template, an OTP will be sent. If you're using phone sign-ins, only an OTP will be sent. You won't be able to send a magiclink for phone sign-ins.\n\nBe aware that you may get back an error message that will not distinguish between the cases where the account does not exist or, that the account can only be accessed via social login.\n\nDo note that you will need to configure a Whatsapp sender on Twilio if you are using phone sign in with the 'whatsapp' channel. The whatsapp channel is not supported on other providers at this time. This method supports PKCE when an email is passed.\n\n- Requires either an email or phone number.\n- This method is used for passwordless sign-ins where a OTP is sent to the user's email or phone number.\n- If the user doesn't exist,&#96;signInWithOtp()&#96; will signup the user instead. To restrict this behavior, you can set&#96;shouldCreateUser&#96; in&#96;SignInWithPasswordlessCredentials.options&#96; to&#96;false&#96;.\n- If you're using an email, you can configure whether you want the user to receive a magiclink or a OTP.\n- If you're using phone, you can configure whether you want the user to receive a OTP.\n- The magic link's destination URL is determined by the [SITE_URL](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/redirect-urls#use-wildcards-in-redirect-urls).\n- See [redirect URLs and wildcards](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/redirect-urls#use-wildcards-in-redirect-urls) to add additional redirect URLs to your project.\n- Magic links and OTPs share the same implementation. To send users a one-time code instead of a magic link, [modify the magic link email template](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/templates) to include&#96;{{ .Token }}&#96; instead of&#96;{{ .ConfirmationURL }}&#96;.\n- See our [Twilio Phone Auth Guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/phone-login?showSMSProvider=Twilio) for details about configuring WhatsApp sign in.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign in with emailSign in with SMS OTPSign in with WhatsApp OTP\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({2  email: 'example@email.com',3  options: {4    emailRedirectTo: 'https://example.com/welcome'5  }6})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Sign in a user through OAuth\n\n&#96;signInWithOAuth(credentials)&#96;\n\nLog in an existing user via a third-party provider. This method supports the PKCE flow.\n\n- This method is used for signing in using [Social Login (OAuth) providers](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth#configure-third-party-providers).\n- It works by redirecting your application to the provider's authorization screen, before bringing back the user to your app.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsSignInWithOAuthCredentials\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign in using a third-party providerSign in using a third-party provider with redirectSign in with scopes and access provider tokens\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({2  provider: 'github'3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Sign in a user through SSO\n\n&#96;signInWithSSO(params)&#96;\n\nAttempts a single-sign on using an enterprise Identity Provider. A successful SSO attempt will redirect the current page to the identity provider authorization page. The redirect URL is implementation and SSO protocol specific.\n\nYou can use it by providing a SSO domain. Typically you can extract this domain by asking users for their email address. If this domain is registered on the Auth instance the redirect will use that organization's currently active SSO Identity Provider for the login.\n\nIf you have built an organization-specific login page, you can use the organization's SSO Identity Provider UUID directly instead.\n\nIn case you need to use a different way to start the authentication flow with an identity provider, you can use the&#96;providerId&#96; property. For example:\n\n- Mapping specific user email addresses with an identity provider.\n- Using different hints to identity the identity provider to be used by the user, like a company-specific page, IP address or other tracking information.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign in with email domainSign in with provider UUID\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1// You can extract the user's email domain and use it to trigger the2  // authentication flow with the correct identity provider.34  const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithSSO({5    domain: 'company.com'6  })78  if (data?.url) {9    // redirect the user to the identity provider's authentication flow10    window.location.href = data.url11  }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Sign in a user through Web3 (Solana, Ethereum)\n\n&#96;signInWithWeb3(credentials)&#96;\n\nSigns in a user by verifying a message signed by the user's private key. Supports Ethereum (via Sign-In-With-Ethereum) \u0026 Solana (Sign-In-With-Solana) standards, both of which derive from the EIP-4361 standard With slight variation on Solana's side.\n\n- Uses a Web3 (Ethereum, Solana) wallet to sign a user in.\n- Read up on the [potential for abuse](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-web3#potential-for-abuse) before using it.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1One of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2One of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign in with Solana or Ethereum (Window API)Sign in with Ethereum (Message and Signature)Sign in with Solana (Brave)Sign in with Solana (Wallet Adapter)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1// uses window.ethereum for the wallet2  const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithWeb3({3    chain: 'ethereum',4    statement: 'I accept the Terms of Service at https://example.com/tos'5  })67  // uses window.solana for the wallet8  const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithWeb3({9    chain: 'solana',10    statement: 'I accept the Terms of Service at https://example.com/tos'11  })\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Get user claims from verified JWT\n\n&#96;getClaims(jwt?, options)&#96;\n\nExtracts the JWT claims present in the access token by first verifying the JWT against the server's JSON Web Key Set endpoint&#96;/.well-known/jwks.json&#96; which is often cached, resulting in significantly faster responses. Prefer this method over #getUser which always sends a request to the Auth server for each JWT.\n\nIf the project is not using an asymmetric JWT signing key (like ECC or RSA) it always sends a request to the Auth server (similar to #getUser) to verify the JWT.\n\n- Parses the user's [access token](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/sessions#access-token-jwt-claims) as a [JSON Web Token (JWT)](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/jwts) and returns its components if valid and not expired.\n- If your project is using asymmetric JWT signing keys, then the verification is done locally usually without a network request using the [WebCrypto API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Crypto_API).\n- A network request is sent to your project's JWT signing key discovery endpoint&#96;https://project-id.supabase.co/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json&#96;, which is cached locally. If your environment is ephemeral, such as a Lambda function that is destroyed after every request, a network request will be sent for each new invocation. Supabase provides a network-edge cache providing fast responses for these situations.\n- If the user's access token is about to expire when calling this function, the user's session will first be refreshed before validating the JWT.\n- If your project is using a symmetric secret to sign the JWT, it always sends a request similar to&#96;getUser()&#96; to validate the JWT at the server before returning the decoded token. This is also used if the WebCrypto API is not available in the environment. Make sure you polyfill it in such situations.\n- The returned claims can be customized per project using the [Custom Access Token Hook](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook).\n\n### Parameters\n\njwt\n\nOptional\n\nstring\n\nAn optional specific JWT you wish to verify, not the one you can obtain from #getSession.\n\noptionsobject\n\nVarious additional options that allow you to customize the behavior of this method.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 3object\n\nDetails\n\nGet JWT claims, header and signature\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.getClaims()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Sign out a user\n\n&#96;signOut(options)&#96;\n\nInside a browser context,&#96;signOut()&#96; will remove the logged in user from the browser session and log them out - removing all items from localstorage and then trigger a&#96;\"SIGNED_OUT\"&#96; event.\n\nFor server-side management, you can revoke all refresh tokens for a user by passing a user's JWT through to&#96;auth.api.signOut(JWT: string)&#96;. There is no way to revoke a user's access token jwt until it expires. It is recommended to set a shorter expiry on the jwt for this reason.\n\nIf using&#96;others&#96; scope, no&#96;SIGNED_OUT&#96; event is fired!\n\n- In order to use the&#96;signOut()&#96; method, the user needs to be signed in first.\n- By default,&#96;signOut()&#96; uses the global scope, which signs out all other sessions that the user is logged into as well. Customize this behavior by passing a scope parameter.\n- Since Supabase Auth uses JWTs for authentication, the access token JWT will be valid until it's expired. When the user signs out, Supabase revokes the refresh token and deletes the JWT from the client-side. This does not revoke the JWT and it will still be valid until it expires.\n\n### Parameters\n\noptionsSignOut\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nSign out (all sessions)Sign out (current session)Sign out (other sessions)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { error } = await supabase.auth.signOut()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Send a password reset request\n\n&#96;resetPasswordForEmail(email, options)&#96;\n\nSends a password reset request to an email address. This method supports the PKCE flow.\n\n- The password reset flow consist of 2 broad steps: (i) Allow the user to login via the password reset link; (ii) Update the user's password.\n- The&#96;resetPasswordForEmail()&#96; only sends a password reset link to the user's email. To update the user's password, see [updateUser()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-updateuser).\n- A&#96;PASSWORD_RECOVERY&#96; event will be emitted when the password recovery link is clicked. You can use [onAuthStateChange()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-onauthstatechange) to listen and invoke a callback function on these events.\n- When the user clicks the reset link in the email they are redirected back to your application. You can configure the URL that the user is redirected to with the&#96;redirectTo&#96; parameter. See [redirect URLs and wildcards](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/redirect-urls#use-wildcards-in-redirect-urls) to add additional redirect URLs to your project.\n- After the user has been redirected successfully, prompt them for a new password and call&#96;updateUser()&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.updateUser({2  password: new_password3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\nemailstring\n\nThe email address of the user.\n\noptionsobject\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nReset passwordReset password (React)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail(email, {2  redirectTo: 'https://example.com/update-password',3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Verify and log in through OTP\n\n&#96;verifyOtp(params)&#96;\n\nLog in a user given a User supplied OTP or TokenHash received through mobile or email.\n\nIf a phone number is used, the type can either be:\n\n1. &#96;sms&#96;– Used when verifying a one-time password (OTP) sent via SMS during sign-up or sign-in.\n2. &#96;phone_change&#96;– Used when verifying an OTP sent to a new phone number during a phone number update process.\n\nIf an email address is used, the type can be one of the following (note:&#96;signup&#96; and&#96;magiclink&#96; types are deprecated):\n\n1. &#96;email&#96;– Used when verifying an OTP sent to the user's email during sign-up or sign-in.\n2. &#96;recovery&#96;– Used when verifying an OTP sent for account recovery, typically after a password reset request.\n3. &#96;invite&#96;– Used when verifying an OTP sent as part of an invitation to join a project or organization.\n4. &#96;email_change&#96;– Used when verifying an OTP sent to a new email address during an email update process.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1VerifyMobileOtpParams\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2VerifyEmailOtpParams\n\nDetails\n\nOption 3VerifyTokenHashParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nVerify Signup One-Time Password (OTP)Verify SMS One-Time Password (OTP)Verify Email Auth (Token Hash)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({ email, token, type: 'email'})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve a session\n\n&#96;getSession()&#96;\n\nReturns the session, refreshing it if necessary.\n\nThe session returned can be null if the session is not detected which can happen in the event a user is not signed-in or has logged out.\n\nIMPORTANT: This method loads values directly from the storage attached to the client. If that storage is based on request cookies for example, the values in it may not be authentic and therefore it's strongly advised against using this method and its results in such circumstances. A warning will be emitted if this is detected. Use #getUser() instead.\n\n- Since the introduction of [asymmetric JWT signing keys](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/signing-keys), this method is considered low-level and we encourage you to use&#96;getClaims()&#96; or&#96;getUser()&#96; instead.\n- Retrieves the current [user session](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/sessions) from the storage medium (local storage, cookies).\n- The session contains an access token (signed JWT), a refresh token and the user object.\n- If the session's access token is expired or is about to expire, this method will use the refresh token to refresh the session.\n- When using in a browser, or you've called&#96;startAutoRefresh()&#96; in your environment (React Native, etc.) this function always returns a valid access token without refreshing the session itself, as this is done in the background. This function returns very fast.\n- IMPORTANT SECURITY NOTICE: If using an insecure storage medium, such as cookies or request headers, the user object returned by this function must not be trusted. Always verify the JWT using&#96;getClaims()&#96; or your own JWT verification library to securely establish the user's identity and access. You can also use&#96;getUser()&#96; to fetch the user object directly from the Auth server for this purpose.\n- When using in a browser, this function is synchronized across all tabs using the [LockManager](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/LockManager) API. In other environments make sure you've defined a proper&#96;lock&#96; property, if necessary, to make sure there are no race conditions while the session is being refreshed.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 3object\n\nDetails\n\nGet the session data\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.getSession()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve a new session\n\n&#96;refreshSession(currentSession?)&#96;\n\nReturns a new session, regardless of expiry status. Takes in an optional current session. If not passed in, then refreshSession() will attempt to retrieve it from getSession(). If the current session's refresh token is invalid, an error will be thrown.\n\n- This method will refresh and return a new session whether the current one is expired or not.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncurrentSession\n\nOptional\n\nobject\n\nThe current session. If passed in, it must contain a refresh token.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nRefresh session using the current sessionRefresh session using a refresh token\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.refreshSession()2const { session, user } = data\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve a user\n\n&#96;getUser(jwt?)&#96;\n\nGets the current user details if there is an existing session. This method performs a network request to the Supabase Auth server, so the returned value is authentic and can be used to base authorization rules on.\n\n- This method fetches the user object from the database instead of local session.\n- This method is useful for checking if the user is authorized because it validates the user's access token JWT on the server.\n- Should always be used when checking for user authorization on the server. On the client, you can instead use&#96;getSession().session.user&#96; for faster results.&#96;getSession&#96; is insecure on the server.\n\n### Parameters\n\njwt\n\nOptional\n\nstring\n\nTakes in an optional access token JWT. If no JWT is provided, the JWT from the current session is used.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nGet the logged in user with the current existing sessionGet the logged in user with a custom access token jwt\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Update a user\n\n&#96;updateUser(attributes, options)&#96;\n\nUpdates user data for a logged in user.\n\n- In order to use the&#96;updateUser()&#96; method, the user needs to be signed in first.\n- By default, email updates sends a confirmation link to both the user's current and new email. To only send a confirmation link to the user's new email, disable Secure email change in your project's [email auth provider settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers).\n\n### Parameters\n\nattributesUserAttributes\n\nDetails\n\noptionsobject\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nUpdate the email for an authenticated userUpdate the phone number for an authenticated userUpdate the password for an authenticated userUpdate the user's metadataUpdate the user's password with a nonce\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.updateUser({2  email: 'new@email.com'3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve identities linked to a user\n\n&#96;getUserIdentities()&#96;\n\nGets all the identities linked to a user.\n\n- The user needs to be signed in to call&#96;getUserIdentities()&#96;.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nReturns a list of identities linked to the user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.getUserIdentities()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Link an identity to a user\n\n&#96;linkIdentity(credentials)&#96;\n\nLinks an oauth identity to an existing user. This method supports the PKCE flow.\n\n- The Enable Manual Linking option must be enabled from your [project's authentication settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers).\n- The user needs to be signed in to call&#96;linkIdentity()&#96;.\n- If the candidate identity is already linked to the existing user or another user,&#96;linkIdentity()&#96; will fail.\n- If&#96;linkIdentity&#96; is run in the browser, the user is automatically redirected to the returned URL. On the server, you should handle the redirect.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1SignInWithOAuthCredentials\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2SignInWithIdTokenCredentials\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nLink an identity to a user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.linkIdentity({2  provider: 'github'3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Unlink an identity from a user\n\n&#96;unlinkIdentity(identity)&#96;\n\nUnlinks an identity from a user by deleting it. The user will no longer be able to sign in with that identity once it's unlinked.\n\n- The Enable Manual Linking option must be enabled from your [project's authentication settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers).\n- The user needs to be signed in to call&#96;unlinkIdentity()&#96;.\n- The user must have at least 2 identities in order to unlink an identity.\n- The identity to be unlinked must belong to the user.\n\n### Parameters\n\nidentityUserIdentity\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nUnlink an identity\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1// retrieve all identities linked to a user2const identities = await supabase.auth.getUserIdentities()34// find the google identity5const googleIdentity = identities.find(6  identity =\u003e identity.provider === 'google'7)89// unlink the google identity10const { error } = await supabase.auth.unlinkIdentity(googleIdentity)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Send a password reauthentication nonce\n\n&#96;reauthenticate()&#96;\n\nSends a reauthentication OTP to the user's email or phone number. Requires the user to be signed-in.\n\n- This method is used together with&#96;updateUser()&#96; when a user's password needs to be updated.\n- If you require your user to reauthenticate before updating their password, you need to enable the Secure password change option in your [project's email provider settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers).\n- A user is only require to reauthenticate before updating their password if Secure password change is enabled and the user hasn't recently signed in. A user is deemed recently signed in if the session was created in the last 24 hours.\n- This method will send a nonce to the user's email. If the user doesn't have a confirmed email address, the method will send the nonce to the user's confirmed phone number instead.\n- After receiving the OTP, include it as the&#96;nonce&#96; in your&#96;updateUser()&#96; call to finalize the password change.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSend reauthentication nonce\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { error } = await supabase.auth.reauthenticate()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Resend an OTP\n\n&#96;resend(credentials)&#96;\n\nResends an existing signup confirmation email, email change email, SMS OTP or phone change OTP.\n\n- Resends a signup confirmation, email change or phone change email to the user.\n- Passwordless sign-ins can be resent by calling the&#96;signInWithOtp()&#96; method again.\n- Password recovery emails can be resent by calling the&#96;resetPasswordForEmail()&#96; method again.\n- This method will only resend an email or phone OTP to the user if there was an initial signup, email change or phone change request being made(note: For existing users signing in with OTP, you should use&#96;signInWithOtp()&#96; again to resend the OTP).\n- You can specify a redirect url when you resend an email link using the&#96;emailRedirectTo&#96; option.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nResend an email signup confirmationResend a phone signup confirmationResend email change emailResend phone change OTP\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { error } = await supabase.auth.resend({2  type: 'signup',3  email: 'email@example.com',4  options: {5    emailRedirectTo: 'https://example.com/welcome'6  }7})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Set the session data\n\n&#96;setSession(currentSession)&#96;\n\nSets the session data from the current session. If the current session is expired, setSession will take care of refreshing it to obtain a new session. If the refresh token or access token in the current session is invalid, an error will be thrown.\n\n- This method sets the session using an&#96;access_token&#96; and&#96;refresh_token&#96;.\n- If successful, a&#96;SIGNED_IN&#96; event is emitted.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncurrentSessionobject\n\nThe current session that minimally contains an access token and refresh token.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSet the session\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.setSession({2    access_token,3    refresh_token4  })\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Exchange an auth code for a session\n\n&#96;exchangeCodeForSession(authCode)&#96;\n\nLog in an existing user by exchanging an Auth Code issued during the PKCE flow.\n\n- Used when&#96;flowType&#96; is set to&#96;pkce&#96; in client options.\n\n### Parameters\n\nauthCodestring\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nExchange Auth Code\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession('34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Start auto-refresh session (non-browser)\n\n&#96;startAutoRefresh()&#96;\n\nStarts an auto-refresh process in the background. The session is checked every few seconds. Close to the time of expiration a process is started to refresh the session. If refreshing fails it will be retried for as long as necessary.\n\nIf you set the GoTrueClientOptions#autoRefreshToken you don't need to call this function, it will be called for you.\n\nOn browsers the refresh process works only when the tab/window is in the foreground to conserve resources as well as prevent race conditions and flooding auth with requests. If you call this method any managed visibility change callback will be removed and you must manage visibility changes on your own.\n\nOn non-browser platforms the refresh process works continuously in the background, which may not be desirable. You should hook into your platform's foreground indication mechanism and call these methods appropriately to conserve resources.\n\n#stopAutoRefresh\n\n- Only useful in non-browser environments such as React Native or Electron.\n- The Supabase Auth library automatically starts and stops proactively refreshing the session when a tab is focused or not.\n- On non-browser platforms, such as mobile or desktop apps built with web technologies, the library is not able to effectively determine whether the application is focused or not.\n- To give this hint to the application, you should be calling this method when the app is in focus and calling&#96;supabase.auth.stopAutoRefresh()&#96; when it's out of focus.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nStart and stop auto refresh in React Native\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1import { AppState } from 'react-native'23// make sure you register this only once!4AppState.addEventListener('change', (state) =\u003e {5  if (state === 'active') {6    supabase.auth.startAutoRefresh()7  } else {8    supabase.auth.stopAutoRefresh()9  }10})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Stop auto-refresh session (non-browser)\n\n&#96;stopAutoRefresh()&#96;\n\nStops an active auto refresh process running in the background (if any).\n\nIf you call this method any managed visibility change callback will be removed and you must manage visibility changes on your own.\n\nSee #startAutoRefresh for more details.\n\n- Only useful in non-browser environments such as React Native or Electron.\n- The Supabase Auth library automatically starts and stops proactively refreshing the session when a tab is focused or not.\n- On non-browser platforms, such as mobile or desktop apps built with web technologies, the library is not able to effectively determine whether the application is focused or not.\n- When your application goes in the background or out of focus, call this method to stop the proactive refreshing of the session.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nStart and stop auto refresh in React Native\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1import { AppState } from 'react-native'23// make sure you register this only once!4AppState.addEventListener('change', (state) =\u003e {5  if (state === 'active') {6    supabase.auth.startAutoRefresh()7  } else {8    supabase.auth.stopAutoRefresh()9  }10})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Initialize client session\n\n&#96;initialize()&#96;\n\nInitializes the client session either from the url or from storage. This method is automatically called when instantiating the client, but should also be called manually when checking for an error from an auth redirect (oauth, magiclink, password recovery, etc).\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Auth MFA\n\nThis section contains methods commonly used for Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and are invoked behind the&#96;supabase.auth.mfa&#96; namespace.\n\nCurrently, there is support for time-based one-time password (TOTP) and phone verification code as the 2nd factor. Recovery codes are not supported but users can enroll multiple factors, with an upper limit of 10.\n\nHaving a 2nd factor for recovery frees the user of the burden of having to store their recovery codes somewhere. It also reduces the attack surface since multiple recovery codes are usually generated compared to just having 1 backup factor.\n\nLearn more about implementing MFA in your application [in the MFA guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa#overview).\n\n---\n\n## Enroll a factor\n\n&#96;enroll(params)&#96;\n\nStarts the enrollment process for a new Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) factor. This method creates a new&#96;unverified&#96; factor. To verify a factor, present the QR code or secret to the user and ask them to add it to their authenticator app. The user has to enter the code from their authenticator app to verify it.\n\nUpon verifying a factor, all other sessions are logged out and the current session's authenticator level is promoted to&#96;aal2&#96;.\n\n- Use&#96;totp&#96; or&#96;phone&#96; as the&#96;factorType&#96; and use the returned&#96;id&#96; to create a challenge.\n- To create a challenge, see [mfa.challenge()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-challenge).\n- To verify a challenge, see [mfa.verify()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-verify).\n- To create and verify a TOTP challenge in a single step, see [mfa.challengeAndVerify()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-challengeandverify).\n- To generate a QR code for the&#96;totp&#96; secret in Next.js, you can do the following:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1\u003cImage src={data.totp.qr_code} alt={data.totp.uri} layout=\"fill\"\u003e\u003c/Image\u003e\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- The&#96;challenge&#96; and&#96;verify&#96; steps are separated when using Phone factors as the user will need time to receive and input the code obtained from the SMS in challenge.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1MFAEnrollTOTPParams\n\nOption 2MFAEnrollPhoneParams\n\nOption 3MFAEnrollParamsBase\n\nOption 4MFAEnrollWebauthnParams\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nEnroll a time-based, one-time password (TOTP) factorEnroll a Phone Factor\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.enroll({2  factorType: 'totp',3  friendlyName: 'your_friendly_name'4})56// Use the id to create a challenge.7// The challenge can be verified by entering the code generated from the authenticator app.8// The code will be generated upon scanning the qr_code or entering the secret into the authenticator app.9const { id, type, totp: { qr_code, secret, uri }, friendly_name } = data10const challenge = await supabase.auth.mfa.challenge({ factorId: id });\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Create a challenge\n\n&#96;challenge(params)&#96;\n\nPrepares a challenge used to verify that a user has access to a MFA factor.\n\n- An [enrolled factor](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-enroll) is required before creating a challenge.\n- To verify a challenge, see [mfa.verify()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-verify).\n- A phone factor sends a code to the user upon challenge. The channel defaults to&#96;sms&#96; unless otherwise specified.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1MFAChallengeParamsBase\n\nOption 2MFAChallengePhoneParams\n\nOption 3MFAChallengeWebauthnParams\n\nOption 4MFAChallengeTOTPParams\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nCreate a challenge for a factorCreate a challenge for a phone factorCreate a challenge for a phone factor (WhatsApp)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.challenge({2  factorId: '34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225'3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Verify a challenge\n\n&#96;verify(params)&#96;\n\nVerifies a code against a challenge. The verification code is provided by the user by entering a code seen in their authenticator app.\n\n- To verify a challenge, please [create a challenge](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-challenge) first.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1MFAVerifyTOTPParams\n\nOption 2MFAVerifyPhoneParams\n\nOption 3MFAVerifyWebauthnParams\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nVerify a challenge for a factor\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.verify({2  factorId: '34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225',3  challengeId: '4034ae6f-a8ce-4fb5-8ee5-69a5863a7c15',4  code: '123456'5})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Create and verify a challenge\n\n&#96;challengeAndVerify(params)&#96;\n\nHelper method which creates a challenge and immediately uses the given code to verify against it thereafter. The verification code is provided by the user by entering a code seen in their authenticator app.\n\n- Intended for use with only TOTP factors.\n- An [enrolled factor](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-enroll) is required before invoking&#96;challengeAndVerify()&#96;.\n- Executes [mfa.challenge()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-challenge) and [mfa.verify()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-verify) in a single step.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsMFAChallengeAndVerifyTOTPParams\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nCreate and verify a challenge for a factor\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.challengeAndVerify({2  factorId: '34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225',3  code: '123456'4})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Unenroll a factor\n\n&#96;unenroll(params)&#96;\n\nUnenroll removes a MFA factor. A user has to have an&#96;aal2&#96; authenticator level in order to unenroll a&#96;verified&#96; factor.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsMFAUnenrollParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nUnenroll a factor\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.unenroll({2  factorId: '34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225',3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Get Authenticator Assurance Level\n\n&#96;getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel(jwt?)&#96;\n\nReturns the Authenticator Assurance Level (AAL) for the active session.\n\n- &#96;aal1&#96;(or&#96;null&#96;) means that the user's identity has been verified only with a conventional login (email+password, OTP, magic link, social login, etc.).\n- &#96;aal2&#96; means that the user's identity has been verified both with a conventional login and at least one MFA factor.\n\nWhen called without a JWT parameter, this method is fairly quick (microseconds) and rarely uses the network. When a JWT is provided (useful in server-side environments like Edge Functions where no session is stored), this method will make a network request to validate the user and fetch their MFA factors.\n\n- Authenticator Assurance Level (AAL) is the measure of the strength of an authentication mechanism.\n- In Supabase, having an AAL of&#96;aal1&#96; refers to having the 1st factor of authentication such as an email and password or OAuth sign-in while&#96;aal2&#96; refers to the 2nd factor of authentication such as a time-based, one-time-password (TOTP) or Phone factor.\n- If the user has a verified factor, the&#96;nextLevel&#96; field will return&#96;aal2&#96;, else, it will return&#96;aal1&#96;.\n- An optional&#96;jwt&#96; parameter can be passed to check the AAL level of a specific JWT instead of the current session.\n\n### Parameters\n\njwt\n\nOptional\n\nstring\n\nTakes in an optional access token JWT. If no JWT is provided, the JWT from the current session is used.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nGet the AAL details of a sessionGet the AAL details for a specific JWT\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel()2const { currentLevel, nextLevel, currentAuthenticationMethods } = data\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## List all factors for current user\n\n&#96;listFactors()&#96;\n\nReturns the list of MFA factors enabled for this user.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## OAuth Server\n\nThe OAuth Server API allows you to build custom OAuth consent screens for your application. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\n---\n\n## Get authorization details\n\n&#96;getAuthorizationDetails(authorizationId)&#96;\n\nRetrieves details about an OAuth authorization request. Used to display consent information to the user. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nThis method returns one of two response types:\n\n- &#96;OAuthAuthorizationDetails&#96;: User needs to consent - show consent page with client info\n- &#96;OAuthRedirect&#96;: User already consented - redirect immediately to the OAuth client\n\nUse type narrowing to distinguish between the responses:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1if ('authorization_id' in data) {2  // Show consent page3} else {4  // Redirect to data.redirect_url5}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\nauthorizationIdstring\n\nThe authorization ID from the authorization request\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Approve authorization\n\n&#96;approveAuthorization(authorizationId, options?)&#96;\n\nApproves an OAuth authorization request. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nAfter approval, the user's consent is stored and an authorization code is generated. The response contains a complete redirect URL with the authorization code and state.\n\n### Parameters\n\nauthorizationIdstring\n\nThe authorization ID to approve\n\noptions\n\nOptional\n\nobject\n\nOptional parameters\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Deny authorization\n\n&#96;denyAuthorization(authorizationId, options?)&#96;\n\nDenies an OAuth authorization request. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nAfter denial, the response contains a redirect URL with an OAuth error (access_denied) to inform the OAuth client that the user rejected the request.\n\n### Parameters\n\nauthorizationIdstring\n\nThe authorization ID to deny\n\noptions\n\nOptional\n\nobject\n\nOptional parameters\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## List grants\n\n&#96;listGrants()&#96;\n\nLists all OAuth grants that the authenticated user has authorized. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Revoke grant\n\n&#96;revokeGrant(options)&#96;\n\nRevokes a user's OAuth grant for a specific client. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nRevocation marks consent as revoked, deletes active sessions for that OAuth client, and invalidates associated refresh tokens.\n\n### Parameters\n\noptionsobject\n\nRevocation options\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Auth Admin\n\n- Any method under the&#96;supabase.auth.admin&#96; namespace requires a&#96;service_role&#96; key.\n- These methods are considered admin methods and should be called on a trusted server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\nCreate server-side auth client\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'23const supabase = createClient(supabase_url, service_role_key, {4  auth: {5    autoRefreshToken: false,6    persistSession: false7  }8})910// Access auth admin api11const adminAuthClient = supabase.auth.admin\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve a user\n\n&#96;getUserById(uid)&#96;\n\nGet user by id.\n\n- Fetches the user object from the database based on the user's id.\n- The&#96;getUserById()&#96; method requires the user's id which maps to the&#96;auth.users.id&#96; column.\n\n### Parameters\n\nuidstring\n\nThe user's unique identifier\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nFetch the user object using the access_token jwt\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.getUserById(1)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## List all users\n\n&#96;listUsers(params?)&#96;\n\nGet a list of users.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n- Defaults to return 50 users per page.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparams\n\nOptional\n\nPageParams\n\nAn object which supports&#96;page&#96; and&#96;perPage&#96; as numbers, to alter the paginated results.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nGet a page of usersPaginated list of users\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data: { users }, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.listUsers()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Create a user\n\n&#96;createUser(attributes)&#96;\n\nCreates a new user. This function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n- To confirm the user's email address or phone number, set&#96;email_confirm&#96; or&#96;phone_confirm&#96; to true. Both arguments default to false.\n- &#96;createUser()&#96; will not send a confirmation email to the user. You can use [inviteUserByEmail()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-admin-inviteuserbyemail) if you want to send them an email invite instead.\n- If you are sure that the created user's email or phone number is legitimate and verified, you can set the&#96;email_confirm&#96; or&#96;phone_confirm&#96; param to&#96;true&#96;.\n\n### Parameters\n\nattributesAdminUserAttributes\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nWith custom user metadataAuto-confirm the user's emailAuto-confirm the user's phone number\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.createUser({2  email: 'user@email.com',3  password: 'password',4  user_metadata: { name: 'Yoda' }5})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Delete a user\n\n&#96;deleteUser(id, shouldSoftDelete)&#96;\n\nDelete a user. Requires a&#96;service_role&#96; key.\n\n- The&#96;deleteUser()&#96; method requires the user's ID, which maps to the&#96;auth.users.id&#96; column.\n\n### Parameters\n\nidstring\n\nThe user id you want to remove.\n\nshouldSoftDeleteboolean\n\nIf true, then the user will be soft-deleted from the auth schema. Soft deletion allows user identification from the hashed user ID but is not reversible. Defaults to false for backward compatibility.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nRemoves a user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.deleteUser(2  '715ed5db-f090-4b8c-a067-640ecee36aa0'3)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Send an email invite link\n\n&#96;inviteUserByEmail(email, options)&#96;\n\nSends an invite link to an email address.\n\n- Sends an invite link to the user's email address.\n- The&#96;inviteUserByEmail()&#96; method is typically used by administrators to invite users to join the application.\n- Note that PKCE is not supported when using&#96;inviteUserByEmail&#96;. This is because the browser initiating the invite is often different from the browser accepting the invite which makes it difficult to provide the security guarantees required of the PKCE flow.\n\n### Parameters\n\nemailstring\n\nThe email address of the user.\n\noptionsobject\n\nAdditional options to be included when inviting.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nInvite a user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail('email@example.com')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Generate an email link\n\n&#96;generateLink(params)&#96;\n\nGenerates email links and OTPs to be sent via a custom email provider.\n\n- The following types can be passed into&#96;generateLink()&#96;:&#96;signup&#96;,&#96;magiclink&#96;,&#96;invite&#96;,&#96;recovery&#96;,&#96;email_change_current&#96;,&#96;email_change_new&#96;,&#96;phone_change&#96;.\n- &#96;generateLink()&#96; only generates the email link for&#96;email_change_email&#96; if the Secure email change is enabled in your project's [email auth provider settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers).\n- &#96;generateLink()&#96; handles the creation of the user for&#96;signup&#96;,&#96;invite&#96; and&#96;magiclink&#96;.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1GenerateSignupLinkParams\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2GenerateInviteOrMagiclinkParams\n\nDetails\n\nOption 3GenerateRecoveryLinkParams\n\nDetails\n\nOption 4GenerateEmailChangeLinkParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nGenerate a signup linkGenerate an invite linkGenerate a magic linkGenerate a recovery linkGenerate links to change current email address\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.generateLink({2  type: 'signup',3  email: 'email@example.com',4  password: 'secret'5})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Update a user\n\n&#96;updateUserById(uid, attributes)&#96;\n\nUpdates the user data. Changes are applied directly without confirmation flows.\n\nImportant: This is a server-side operation and does not trigger client-side&#96;onAuthStateChange&#96; listeners. The admin API has no connection to client state.\n\nTo sync changes to the client after calling this method:\n\n1. On the client, call&#96;supabase.auth.refreshSession()&#96; to fetch the updated user data\n2. This will trigger the&#96;TOKEN_REFRESHED&#96; event and notify all listeners\n\n### Parameters\n\nuidstring\n\nThe user's unique identifier\n\nattributesAdminUserAttributes\n\nThe data you want to update.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nExample 1Updates a user's emailUpdates a user's passwordUpdates a user's metadataUpdates a user's app_metadataConfirms a user's email addressConfirms a user's phone numberBan a user for 100 years\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1// Server-side (Edge Function)2const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.updateUserById(3  userId,4  { user_metadata: { preferences: { theme: 'dark' } } }5)67// Client-side (to sync the changes)8const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.refreshSession()9// onAuthStateChange listeners will now be notified with updated user\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Sign out a user (admin)\n\n&#96;signOut(jwt, scope)&#96;\n\nRemoves a logged-in session.\n\n### Parameters\n\njwtstring\n\nA valid, logged-in JWT.\n\nscopeOne of the following options\n\nThe logout sope.\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1\"global\"\n\nOption 2\"local\"\n\nOption 3\"others\"\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Delete a factor for a user\n\n&#96;deleteFactor(params)&#96;\n\nDeletes a factor on a user. This will log the user out of all active sessions if the deleted factor was verified.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsAuthMFAAdminDeleteFactorParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nDelete a factor for a user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.mfa.deleteFactor({2  id: '34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225',3  userId: 'a89baba7-b1b7-440f-b4bb-91026967f66b',4})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## List all factors for a user (admin)\n\n&#96;listFactors(params)&#96;\n\nLists all factors associated to a user.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsAuthMFAAdminListFactorsParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nList all factors for a user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.mfa.listFactors()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## OAuth Admin\n\nThe OAuth Admin API allows you to manage OAuth clients programmatically. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth. These functions should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n---\n\n## List OAuth clients\n\n&#96;listClients(params?)&#96;\n\nLists all OAuth clients with optional pagination. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparams\n\nOptional\n\nPageParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Get OAuth client\n\n&#96;getClient(clientId)&#96;\n\nGets details of a specific OAuth client. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n### Parameters\n\nclientIdstring\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Create OAuth client\n\n&#96;createClient(params)&#96;\n\nCreates a new OAuth client. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsCreateOAuthClientParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Update OAuth client\n\n&#96;updateClient(clientId, params)&#96;\n\nUpdates an existing OAuth client. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n### Parameters\n\nclientIdstring\n\nparamsUpdateOAuthClientParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Delete OAuth client\n\n&#96;deleteClient(clientId)&#96;\n\nDeletes an OAuth client. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n### Parameters\n\nclientIdstring\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Regenerate client secret\n\n&#96;regenerateClientSecret(clientId)&#96;\n\nRegenerates the secret for an OAuth client. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n### Parameters\n\nclientIdstring\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Invokes a Supabase Edge Function.\n\n&#96;invoke(functionName, options)&#96;\n\nInvokes a function\n\n- Requires an Authorization header.\n- Invoke params generally match the [Fetch API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API) spec.\n- When you pass in a body to your function, we automatically attach the Content-Type header for&#96;Blob&#96;,&#96;ArrayBuffer&#96;,&#96;File&#96;,&#96;FormData&#96; and&#96;String&#96;. If it doesn't match any of these types we assume the payload is&#96;json&#96;, serialize it and attach the&#96;Content-Type&#96; header as&#96;application/json&#96;. You can override this behavior by passing in a&#96;Content-Type&#96; header of your own.\n- Responses are automatically parsed as&#96;json&#96;,&#96;blob&#96; and&#96;form-data&#96; depending on the&#96;Content-Type&#96; header sent by your function. Responses are parsed as&#96;text&#96; by default.\n\n### Parameters\n\nfunctionNamestring\n\nThe name of the Function to invoke.\n\noptionsFunctionInvokeOptions\n\nOptions for invoking the Function.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1FunctionsResponseSuccess\n\nOption 2FunctionsResponseFailure\n\nExample 1Basic invocationError handlingPassing custom headersCalling with DELETE HTTP verbInvoking a Function in the UsEast1 regionCalling with GET HTTP verbExample 7\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await functions.invoke('hello-world', {2  body: { name: 'Ada' },3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## CORS headers for Edge Functions\n\nDefault CORS headers for Supabase Edge Functions.\n\nIncludes all headers sent by Supabase client libraries and allows all standard HTTP methods. Use this for simple CORS configurations with wildcard origin.\n\nBasic usage\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1import { corsHeaders } from '@supabase/supabase-js/cors'23Deno.serve(async (req) =\u003e {4  if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {5    return new Response('ok', { headers: corsHeaders })6  }78  return new Response(9    JSON.stringify({ data: 'Hello' }),10    { headers: { ...corsHeaders, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }11  )12})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Update authorization token\n\n&#96;setAuth(token)&#96;\n\nUpdates the authorization header\n\n### Parameters\n\ntokenstring\n\nthe new jwt token sent in the authorisation header\n\n### Return Type\n\nvoid\n\nSetting the authorization header\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1functions.setAuth(session.access_token)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Subscribe to channel\n\n&#96;on(type, filter, callback)&#96;\n\nCreates an event handler that listens to changes.\n\n- By default, Broadcast and Presence are enabled for all projects.\n- By default, listening to database changes is disabled for new projects due to database performance and security concerns. You can turn it on by managing Realtime's [replication](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api#realtime-api-overview).\n- You can receive the \"previous\" data for updates and deletes by setting the table's&#96;REPLICA IDENTITY&#96; to&#96;FULL&#96;(e.g.,&#96;ALTER TABLE your_table REPLICA IDENTITY FULL;&#96;).\n- Row level security is not applied to delete statements. When RLS is enabled and replica identity is set to full, only the primary key is sent to clients.\n\n### Parameters\n\ntypeOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1\"presence\"\n\nOption 2\"postgres_changes\"\n\nOption 3\"broadcast\"\n\nOption 4\"system\"\n\nfilterOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 3object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 4object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 5RealtimePostgresChangesFilter\n\nDetails\n\nOption 6RealtimePostgresChangesFilter\n\nDetails\n\nOption 7RealtimePostgresChangesFilter\n\nDetails\n\nOption 8RealtimePostgresChangesFilter\n\nDetails\n\nOption 9RealtimePostgresChangesFilter\n\nDetails\n\nOption 10object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 11object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 12object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 13object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 14object\n\nDetails\n\ncallbackfunction\n\nDetails\n\nListen to broadcast messagesListen to presence syncListen to presence joinListen to presence leaveListen to all database changesListen to a specific tableListen to insertsListen to updatesListen to deletesListen to multiple eventsListen to row level changes\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const channel = supabase.channel(\"room1\")23channel.on(\"broadcast\", { event: \"cursor-pos\" }, (payload) =\u003e {4  console.log(\"Cursor position received!\", payload);5}).subscribe((status) =\u003e {6  if (status === \"SUBSCRIBED\") {7    channel.send({8      type: \"broadcast\",9      event: \"cursor-pos\",10      payload: { x: Math.random(), y: Math.random() },11    });12  }13});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Unsubscribe from a channel\n\n&#96;removeChannel(channel)&#96;\n\nUnsubscribes and removes Realtime channel from Realtime client.\n\n- Removing a channel is a great way to maintain the performance of your project's Realtime service as well as your database if you're listening to Postgres changes. Supabase will automatically handle cleanup 30 seconds after a client is disconnected, but unused channels may cause degradation as more clients are simultaneously subscribed.\n\n### Parameters\n\nchannelRealtimeChannel\n\nThe name of the Realtime channel.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1\"error\"\n\nOption 2\"ok\"\n\nOption 3\"timed out\"\n\nRemoves a channel\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1supabase.removeChannel(myChannel)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Unsubscribe from all channels\n\n&#96;removeAllChannels()&#96;\n\nUnsubscribes and removes all Realtime channels from Realtime client.\n\n- Removing channels is a great way to maintain the performance of your project's Realtime service as well as your database if you're listening to Postgres changes. Supabase will automatically handle cleanup 30 seconds after a client is disconnected, but unused channels may cause degradation as more clients are simultaneously subscribed.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \u003e\n\nDetails\n\nRemove all channels\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1supabase.removeAllChannels()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve all channels\n\n&#96;getChannels()&#96;\n\nReturns all Realtime channels.\n\n### Return Type\n\nArray \n\nGet all channels\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const channels = supabase.getChannels()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Broadcast a message\n\n&#96;send(args, opts)&#96;\n\nSends a message into the channel.\n\n- When using REST you don't need to subscribe to the channel\n- REST calls are only available from 2.37.0 onwards\n\n### Parameters\n\nargsobject\n\nArguments to send to channel\n\nDetails\n\nopts{ [key: string]: any }\n\nOptions to be used during the send process\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1\"ok\"\n\nOption 2\"timed out\"\n\nOption 3\"error\"\n\nSend a message via websocketSend a message via REST\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const channel = supabase.channel('room1')23channel.subscribe((status) =\u003e {4  if (status === 'SUBSCRIBED') {5    channel.send({6      type: 'broadcast',7      event: 'cursor-pos',8      payload: { x: Math.random(), y: Math.random() },9    })10  }11})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Set authentication token\n\n&#96;setAuth(token)&#96;\n\nSets the JWT access token used for channel subscription authorization and Realtime RLS.\n\nIf param is null it will use the&#96;accessToken&#96; callback function or the token set on the client.\n\nOn callback used, it will set the value of the token internal to the client.\n\nWhen a token is explicitly provided, it will be preserved across channel operations (including removeChannel and resubscribe). The&#96;accessToken&#96; callback will not be invoked until&#96;setAuth()&#96; is called without arguments.\n\n### Parameters\n\ntokenOne of the following options\n\nA JWT string to override the token set on the client.\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1null\n\nOption 2string\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nExample 1\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1Setting the authorization header2// Use a manual token (preserved across resubscribes, ignores accessToken callback)3client.realtime.setAuth('my-custom-jwt')45// Switch back to using the accessToken callback6client.realtime.setAuth()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## File Buckets\n\nThis section contains methods for working with File Buckets.\n\n---\n\n## Access a storage bucket\n\n&#96;from(id)&#96;\n\nPerform file operation in a bucket.\n\n### Parameters\n\nidstring\n\nThe bucket id to operate on.\n\nAccessing a bucket\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const avatars = supabase.storage.from('avatars')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## List all buckets\n\n&#96;listBuckets(options?)&#96;\n\nRetrieves the details of all Storage buckets within an existing project.\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions:&#96;select&#96;\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions: none\n\n### Parameters\n\noptions\n\nOptional\n\nListBucketOptions\n\nQuery parameters for listing buckets\n\nDetails\n\n- Refer to the [Storage guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control) on how access control works\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nList bucketsList buckets with options\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .storage3  .listBuckets()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve a bucket\n\n&#96;getBucket(id)&#96;\n\nRetrieves the details of an existing Storage bucket.\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions:&#96;select&#96;\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions: none\n\n### Parameters\n\nidstring\n\nThe unique identifier of the bucket you would like to retrieve.\n\n- Refer to the [Storage guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control) on how access control works\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nGet bucket\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .storage3  .getBucket('avatars')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Create a bucket\n\n&#96;createBucket(id, options)&#96;\n\nCreates a new Storage bucket\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions:&#96;insert&#96;\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions: none\n\n### Parameters\n\nidstring\n\nA unique identifier for the bucket you are creating.\n\noptionsobject\n\nDetails\n\n- Refer to the [Storage guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control) on how access control works\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nCreate bucket\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .storage3  .createBucket('avatars', {4    public: false,5    allowedMimeTypes: ['image/png'],6    fileSizeLimit: 10247  })\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Empty a bucket\n\n&#96;emptyBucket(id)&#96;\n\nRemoves all objects inside a single bucket.\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions:&#96;select&#96;\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions:&#96;select&#96; and&#96;delete&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\nidstring\n\nThe unique identifier of the bucket you would like to empty.\n\n- Refer to the [Storage guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control) on how access control works\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nEmpty bucket\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .storage3  .emptyBucket('avatars')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Update a bucket\n\n&#96;updateBucket(id, options)&#96;\n\nUpdates a Storage bucket\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions:&#96;select&#96; and&#96;update&#96;\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions: none\n\n### Parameters\n\nidstring\n\nA unique identifier for the bucket you are updating.\n\noptionsobject\n\nDetails\n\n- Refer to the [Storage guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control) on how access control works\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nUpdate bucket\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .storage3  .updateBucket('avatars', {4    public: false,5    allowedMimeTypes: ['image/png'],6    fileSizeLimit: 10247  })\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Delete a bucket\n\n&#96;deleteBucket(id)&#96;\n\nDeletes an existing bucket. A bucket can't be deleted with existing objects inside it. You must first&#96;empty()&#96; the bucket.\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions:&#96;select&#96; and&#96;delete&#96;\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions: none\n\n### Parameters\n\nidstring\n\nThe unique identifier of the bucket you would like to delete.\n\n- Refer to the [Storage guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control) on how access control works\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nDelete bucket\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .storage3  .deleteBucket('avatars')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Upload a file\n\n&#96;upload(path, fileBody, fileOptions?)&#96;\n\nUploads a file to an existing bucket.\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions: none\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions: only&#96;insert&#96; when you are uploading new files and&#96;select&#96;,&#96;insert&#96; and&#96;update&#96; when you are upserting files\n\n### Parameters\n\npathstring\n\nThe file path, including the file name. Should be of the format&#96;folder/subfolder/filename.png&#96;. The bucket must already exist before attempting to upload.\n\nfileBodyFileBody\n\nThe body of the file to be stored in the bucket.\n\nfileOptions\n\nOptional\n\nFileOptions\n\nOptional file upload options including cacheControl, contentType, upsert, and metadata.\n\nDetails\n\n- For React Native, using either&#96;Blob&#96;,&#96;File&#96; or&#96;FormData&#96; does not work as intended. Upload file using&#96;ArrayBuffer&#96; from base64 file data instead, see example below.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nUpload fileUpload file using &#96;ArrayBuffer&#96; from base64 file data\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const avatarFile = event.target.files[0]2const { data, error } = await supabase3  .storage4  .from('avatars')5  .upload('public/avatar1.png', avatarFile, {6    cacheControl: '3600',7    upsert: false8  })\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Replace an existing file\n\n&#96;update(path, fileBody, fileOptions?)&#96;\n\nReplaces an existing file at the specified path with a new one.\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions: none\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions:&#96;update&#96; and&#96;select&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\npathstring\n\nThe relative file path. Should be of the format&#96;folder/subfolder/filename.png&#96;. The bucket must already exist before attempting to update.\n\nfileBodyOne of the following options\n\nThe body of the file to be stored in the bucket.\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1string\n\nOption 2ArrayBuffer\n\nOption 3ReadableStream\n\nOption 4Blob\n\nOption 5File\n\nOption 6FormData\n\nOption 7@types/node.__global.NodeJS.ReadableStream\n\nOption 8URLSearchParams\n\nOption 9ArrayBufferView\n\nOption 10@types/node.__global.Buffer\n\nfileOptions\n\nOptional\n\nFileOptions\n\nOptional file upload options including cacheControl, contentType, upsert, and metadata.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nUpdate fileUpdate file using &#96;ArrayBuffer&#96; from base64 file data\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const avatarFile = event.target.files[0]2const { data, error } = await supabase3  .storage4  .from('avatars')5  .update('public/avatar1.png', avatarFile, {6    cacheControl: '3600',7    upsert: true8  })\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Move an existing file\n\n&#96;move(fromPath, toPath, options?)&#96;\n\nMoves an existing file to a new path in the same bucket.\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions: none\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions:&#96;update&#96; and&#96;select&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\nfromPathstring\n\nThe original file path, including the current file name. For example&#96;folder/image.png&#96;.\n\ntoPathstring\n\nThe new file path, including the new file name. For example&#96;folder/image-new.png&#96;.\n\noptions\n\nOptional\n\nDestinationOptions\n\nThe destination options.\n\nDetails\n\n- Refer to the [Storage guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control) on how access control works\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nMove file\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .storage3  .from('avatars')4  .move('public/avatar1.png', 'private/avatar2.png')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Copy an existing file\n\n&#96;copy(fromPath, toPath, options?)&#96;\n\nCopies an existing file to a new path in the same bucket.\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions: none\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions:&#96;insert&#96; and&#96;select&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\nfromPathstring\n\nThe original file path, including the current file name. For example&#96;folder/image.png&#96;.\n\ntoPathstring\n\nThe new file path, including the new file name. For example&#96;folder/image-copy.png&#96;.\n\noptions\n\nOptional\n\nDestinationOptions\n\nThe destination options.\n\nDetails\n\n- Refer to the [Storage guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control) on how access control works\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nCopy file\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .storage3  .from('avatars')4  .copy('public/avatar1.png', 'private/avatar2.png')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Create a signed URL\n\n&#96;createSignedUrl(path, expiresIn, options?)&#96;\n\nCreates a signed URL. Use a signed URL to share a file for a fixed amount of time.\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions: none\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions:&#96;select&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\npathstring\n\nThe file path, including the current file name. For example&#96;folder/image.png&#96;.\n\nexpiresInnumber\n\nThe number of seconds until the signed URL expires. For example,&#96;60&#96; for a URL which is valid for one minute.\n\noptions\n\nOptional\n\nobject\n\nDetails\n\n- Refer to the [Storage guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control) on how access control works\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nCreate Signed URLCreate a signed URL for an asset with transformationsCreate a signed URL which triggers the download of the asset\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .storage3  .from('avatars')4  .createSignedUrl('folder/avatar1.png', 60)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Create signed URLs\n\n&#96;createSignedUrls(paths, expiresIn, options?)&#96;\n\nCreates multiple signed URLs. Use a signed URL to share a file for a fixed amount of time.\n\nRLS policy permissions required:\n\n- &#96;buckets&#96; table permissions: none\n- &#96;objects&#96; table permissions:&#96;select&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\npathsArray \n\nThe file paths to be downloaded, including the current file names. For example&#96;['folder/image.png', 'folder2/image2.png']&#96;.\n\nexpiresInnumber\n\nThe number of seconds until the signed URLs expire. For example,&#96;60&#96; for URLs which are valid for one minute.\n\noptions\n\nOptional\n\nobject\n\nDetails\n\n- Refer to the [Storage guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control) on how access control works\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nCreate Signed URLs\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .storage3  .from('avatars')4  .createSignedUrls(['folder/avatar1.png', 'folder/avatar2.png'], 60)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Create signed upload URL\n\n&#96;createSignedUploadUrl(path, options?)&#96;\n\nCreates a signed upload URL.
